title: Push-off peak discriminates gait pathology, certified: healthy highest, calcaneus lowest across five classes (Kruskal-Wallis H bit-for-bit vs base R, machine-precision vs scipy)

dataset.name: GaitRec -- large-scale ground reaction force dataset of healthy and impaired gait
dataset.record: vertical GRF (processed, BW- and time-normalised), push-off peak (grfLandmarks 3rd landmark); five gait classes: healthy control (n=208), ankle (n=483), knee (n=499), hip (n=364), calcaneus (n=290)
dataset.citation: Horsak B, Slijepcevic D, Raberger AM, Schwab C, Worisch M, Zeppelzauer M. GaitRec, a large-scale ground reaction force dataset of healthy and impaired gait. Scientific Data 2020;7:143. doi:10.1038/s41597-020-0481-z.

proposition: The ANOVA sibling showed the vGRF dynamic range clusters the four pathology classes together; a different landmark -- the push-off peak (late-stance propulsion) -- separates them. Because the push-off peak is right-skewed, the distribution-free Kruskal-Wallis test is the appropriate omnibus. Each subject's push-off peak comes from the certified grfLandmarks; the NEWLY-AUTHORED kruskalTest compares the five classes, reproducing base R stats::kruskal.test BIT-FOR-BIT and scipy.stats.kruskal to machine precision. The push-off peak differs across classes (H=274.5, df=4, p~3.5e-58); by mean rank healthy controls have the largest push-off (1408; 1.102 BW) and calcaneus pathology the smallest (632; 1.008 BW), ankle/knee/hip in between -- a propulsion deficit that discriminates the pathology classes.

claims.statement: tie-corrected Kruskal-Wallis H of the vertical-GRF push-off peak across the five gait classes
-log10(omnibus p): the group difference is overwhelmingly significant
mean rank of healthy controls (the largest push-off, highest rank)
mean rank of calcaneus pathology (the smallest push-off, lowest rank)
healthy controls have the highest mean push-off rank of the five classes
calcaneus pathology has the lowest mean push-off rank (worst propulsion)

validation.reference: The newly-authored kruskalTest op (tie-corrected non-parametric between-groups omnibus) is validated against BOTH scipy.stats.kruskal AND base R stats::kruskal.test on the identical five groups -- a double reference. All three compute the Kruskal-Wallis H of the vGRF push-off peak across the five classes; base R kruskal.test agrees BIT-FOR-BIT (|diff| = 0; the H is accumulated in the identical FP order) and scipy agrees to machine precision (|diff| ~ 9e-13, floating-point associativity). The per-subject push-off peaks come from PhysioMoCap::grfLandmarks (3rd landmark; certified in the sibling gait-grf-gaitrec case). The per-class mean ranks are reported.
validation.data: REAL -- GaitRec (Horsak et al. 2020), processed vertical GRF push-off peak, five gait classes: healthy control (n=208), ankle (n=483), knee (n=499), hip (n=364), calcaneus (n=290)
validation.note: The reproducible findings are (1) kruskalTest reproduces base R kruskal.test bit-for-bit and scipy.stats.kruskal to machine precision on the 5-class push-off cohort; (2) the push-off peak discriminates gait pathology, healthy highest and calcaneus lowest. HONEST scope: (1) this AUTHORS A NEW OP, kruskalTest (the non-parametric, distribution-free counterpart of the certified oneWayAnova), and reuses the certified grfLandmarks op (validated in the sibling gait-grf-gaitrec case) for the push-off peak (its 3rd landmark); (2) the tie-corrected Kruskal-Wallis H reproduces base R stats::kruskal.test BIT-FOR-BIT (|diff| = 0; the H is accumulated in the identical FP order) and scipy.stats.kruskal to MACHINE PRECISION (|diff| ~ 9e-13, floating-point associativity), so base R is the exact reference and scipy the machine-precision cross-check; (3) the Kruskal-Wallis test is used because the push-off peak is RIGHT-SKEWED (skew ~ +0.35 pooled, up to +0.6 within classes), so the distribution-free omnibus is more appropriate than a normal-theory ANOVA; (4) the finding: the push-off peak differs across the five classes -- H = 274.5 on 4 df, p ~ 3.5e-58 -- and by mean rank healthy controls have the LARGEST push-off (rank 1407.5; mean 1.102 BW) and CALCANEUS pathology the SMALLEST (rank 632.2; mean 1.008 BW), with ankle (838.9), knee (931.0) and hip (975.8) in between; unlike the dynamic range (which clustered the four pathology classes near 0.22 BW), the push-off peak DISCRIMINATES the pathology classes, and the calcaneus group's propulsion deficit is the most severe -- biomechanically sensible, since push-off is chiefly an ankle-plantarflexor action; (5) a real cross-sectional cohort (ASSOCIATION, NOT CAUSATION), one processed vGRF per subject, initial-presentation baseline sessions; run_simulation = FALSE (deterministic).

open_questions.q: The omnibus certifies that the five classes differ in push-off, with a clear healthy-highest, calcaneus-lowest ordering; post-hoc pairwise tests (e.g. Dunn) would establish which specific class pairs differ, and combining the push-off peak with the loading peak and mid-stance trough (a multivariate GRF-landmark profile) would give a fuller pathology fingerprint. The single push-off peak shown here is the most interpretable propulsion read-out. Documented, not escalated.
